newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Verbund sees stable earnings mid-term.
newsitem.headline: Verbund sees stable earnings mid-term.

text.p: Austrian national grid company Verbund said on Monday it expected stable earnings in the medium term although liberalised electricity markets from 1999 would lead to tougher competition among utilities.

"Cash flow should be around six billion schillings and in the mid-term we will be in a very favourable competitive position with our fully depreciated hydro power plants," chief financial officer Michael Pistauer told a news conference.
Cash flow was about six billion schillings in 1996 down from 6.14 billion the previous year.
"We do not fear competition in the coming liberalised markets," chief executive Hans Haider said.

Verbund said it expected to hold its own in an increasingly competitive environment thanks to a new operating structure, that breaks up the group into divisions for electricity generation, distribution, sales and new business.
Haider said he doubted whether prices would come under much pressure when the market opened up in 1999.

"If you look closely at prices in Germany or Italy then we are in a favourable position," Haider said. He admitted, however, that there would be some price pressure from big industrial clients as a result of liberalisation.

Verbund, which generates more than half of Austria's electricity, and the provincial utilities have already agreed on a "risk sharing" model in order to spread out any burden arising from liberalisation, Haider said.
"Rationalisation will be an ongoing subject," he said.
The firm reduced its staff in 1996 by 3.5 percent to 4,650 and Verbund wanted to cut another 150 this year, Haider said.
Automation of plants would also continue, he said.
Verbund earlier reported an eight percent increase in 1996 pre-tax profit helped by an improved financial result while net profit fell slightly to 1.34 billion from 1.38 billion schillings.
Verbund's sales revenues climbed 1.8 percent to around 20 billion schillings but overall electricity sales were down 2.4 percent due to a drop in exports by 22 percent.
Results in 1997 would be in line with last year but Pistauer declined to give further details.
As investments in fixed assets would decline in the next years, Verbund would use its free cash flow to reduce its liabilities, Pistauer said. --- Christian Gutlederer +43 1 531 12 275
